title: Austin: Auditorium, Oil, & Thanksgiving Spirit
summary:
*   **City Auditorium Agreement:** The city approved a $500 payment to the Retail Merchants' Association, settling financial claims related to their joint ownership of the City Auditorium building.
*   **New Filling Station Approved:** A permit was granted to the Oriental Oil Company for the erection of a new filling station, reflecting the growing automotive presence in the city.
*   **Thanksgiving Patriotic Program:** Plans were discussed to organize a patriotic musical program for Thanksgiving Day, engaging the community in post-World War I celebrations.

APPROVED, Nov. 21, 1918: A. P. Wooldridge, Mayor.
James F. Moore of the War Camp Community Service was present and discussed with the Mayor
the matter of cooperation in the preparation of a patriotic musical program for the
afternoon of Thanksgiving day.
There was laid before the Council a petition of the Oriental Oil Company for the privilege
of erecting a filling station on the property known as the Wolf Estate "in the southeast
corner of Block Second and Congress avenue," and the Council voted by 5 yeas, no nays, to
grant the permit.
